back: A place, structure or object of historical, cultural or natural importance protected by law for the whole nation, e.g. Great Zimbabwe.
A sacred place where people honour the dead or worship and pray, e.g. the National Heroes Acre or Njelele.

front: Which body protects national monuments in Zimbabwe?
back: National Museums and Monuments of Zimbabwe (NMMZ).

front: Where is the National Heroes Acre?
Name four national monuments in Zimbabwe.
back: Any four of: Great Zimbabwe, Khami, Naletale, Danangombe, Ziwa, Chinhoyi Caves, Domboshava.
A shrine of the Mwari/Mwali religion in the Matobo Hills, used for rain-asking and other rituals.

front: Why are monuments and shrines significant?
back: They are evidence of history, build identity and pride, are places of worship and remembrance, bring tourism income and are used for education and research.
Any four of: vandalism and graffiti, theft of artefacts, fire, weathering and erosion, plants growing into walls, too many visitors, nearby mining or development.

front: How can citizens help protect heritage sites?
back: Visit respectfully, keep to paths, never write on or remove anything, and report damage to the authorities or traditional leaders.
